answer.answer: Audit-ready takeover completed. The import remains a preserved external research package; the canonical game-data snapshot was not duplicated. Checkpoint persisted as `checkpoint:f8731400-1782-f52e-56a0-3cd6f4e806a0`.

claims.value: The lossless import preserves the original 21,674,717-byte `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` (SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`) and verified extracted tree under Git-ignored `raw/`. The ZIP contains 123 entries including directories; all 115 manifested files passed ZIP, package-manifest, and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` validation. The tracked `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` retain the audit trail. The package was supplied on 2026-07-11, imported at `2026-07-11T19:54:52Z`, and its data retrieval boundary is `2026-07-08T19:01:37Z`. The ignored raw material intentionally retains the duplicate third-party corpus, personalized save context, generated binaries, legacy SQLite database, source snapshot JSON, delivery CSVs, workbook, refresh script, and query script without making them active pipeline state.

The archive’s repeated implication that its numeric data is Steam build `23761620` is incorrect: `0.2.8`/`23761620` was only the latest public executable observed, not proven provenance for every value. The correct two-axis boundary is (1) game-data claim: Update 1, internal game version `35118973`, dated 2026-04-09 and contextually mapped to Steam build `22674441` (inferred `0.2.0`); and (2) source snapshot: SRDB `2.3.4`, updated 2026-07-10 and retrieved `2026-07-11 05:02:30 UTC`. The immutable canonical snapshot is `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`. The archive’s source-site version and reliable numeric-data build claim were not recorded, so its imported numeric reports remain legacy calculations until ported and rerun against that canonical snapshot; they must not be relabeled with its ID beforehand.

Reconciliation found the archive’s 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot rows, and official-news subset semantically duplicated the richer RuptureOps corpus, so none was installed as a competing canonical snapshot. Distinct evidence was promoted selectively: `models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json`; six medium-confidence Ore Excavator v2 impure/pure recipe-producer associations in `sources/recipe-producer-overrides.json`; explicit medium-confidence consumable-effect assumptions with provenance warnings in `sources/consumable-effects.json`; nine player-specific site/geography assets; and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. The reconciliation also corrected the `airlock` item overwritten by a building-shaped response and Training Corporation’s literal `$undefined` index. Duplicate prompt material was preserved intact as provenance but promoted only once: formatting variants and overlapping prefixes did not become duplicate facts, questions were not treated as answers, quoted assistant recommendations were not promoted as player observations, and plans were kept distinct from installed state. No second canonical game-data snapshot was created.

The complete 18-file `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` family is retained strictly as `superseded_audit_only`: the player explicitly rejected its buffer-heavy direction, and it must not become current guidance. The July 11 authority is `Topics/StarRupture/Player save - progression and next builds.md`, whose staged Flowworks build is a current adopted plan—not confirmed construction. It starts with one Titanium Excavator, one Wolfram Excavator, one Titanium Smelter, one Wolfram Smelter, Titanium Rod v2, Wolfram Powder v2, Wolfram Plate v2, one Stabilizer, one Impeller, and one Turbine. The Valve expansion adds one Titanium Smelter, Sheet v2, Beam, Housing, Nozzle, and two Valves, adding a second v1 Titanium Excavator only for an Impure node. Two Pumps follow for the Pressure Tank pack; the second Stabilizer is delayed until before Scanner/levels 11–12; and one HRS v2 pad is reserved but built only if imported-HRS recovery fails in practice. The active RuptureOps corpus, pipeline, database, and immutable snapshot remain authoritative over the preserved archive database, reports, and scripts.

answer.answer: Landmark-grounded geography established and persisted as checkpoint `checkpoint:571f21bb-43c4-a31f-eac9-ab8ad66d9378`.

claims.value: The older provisional Grand Basin match to the Red Lake/Redleaf basin was wrong. The canonical Grand Basin Reserve is north of the active production corridor, immediately east of GRO “Mythic Cry” in the adjacent basin; its marker denotes the basin area, not a future Core.

Flowworks is the selected site between Landerworks and Faraday: east/northeast of Landerworks and west/northwest of Faraday. It belongs to the existing western-to-eastern production corridor but remains a proposed footprint, not a placed Core.

North is up on the named map, but its dashed site axis and overview pins express visually terrain-registered relationships rather than surveyed geometry. Planning-note coordinates identify SRDB markers. No verified transform connects the screenshot-registration frame to SRDB coordinates, so they must remain separate; prefer landmark-relative directions and do not present relational pins as exact coordinates.

The preferred first permanent Goethite satellite is the safer northwestern triple at approximately `1393–1464,1838–1891`, northwest of Mythic Cry/Grand Basin. The closer western field around `1252–1472,2950–3282` is not preferred because it overlaps scanner/hostile envelopes. Build all three Laser Drills, merge them into one Goethite-only Cargo Dispatcher, receive 45 raw Ore/min into a 1,600-unit Storage Depot v2, charge the buffer, and initially operate only the required Pyro Forges. A geographically separate fourth drill is strictly an empty-buffer fallback and requires its own Dispatcher/Receiver pair. The preferred first Oil satellite is approximately `1234,3760`, west/southwest of Mythic Cry and Grand Basin: start with one Oil Extractor and one Crude-only Dispatcher/Receiver pair delivering 10 Crude/min into one V2 buffer for one GB-A Refinery. Reserve—but do not initially build—a second pair and Refinery because one Refinery already consumes the entire 10 Crude/min source plus large Titanium and Calcium feeds; the second marker around `1351,4473` is a separate site, not a same-pad extension. Both choices move compact raw resources through item-specific Cargo links for processing beside Grand Basin consumers, avoiding world-trunk transport of expanded intermediates.

answer.answer: Duplicate forks are coordinated around one verified archive identity and one continuation checkpoint. Exact promotion-receipt and dirty-file inventories were not present in the available evidence and remain explicitly unresolved.

claims.value: The topology contains seven related tasks: `019f4f6d-169c-70e2-8de4-81722b41eee9` (initial Update 1 research/bootstrap), `019f5263-8bae-7d10-b944-0fd4a543afb9` (clean bootstrap and ownership split), `019f52a5-72aa-7c11-853c-5de258361b42` (general import/reconciliation), `019f52fa-6195-7701-96a2-da6ec7ef7a08` (live exploration continuation), `019f52fa-6917-78a3-b1e5-7e631263b4a5` (logistics fork), `019f52fa-7180-7552-a3b1-09be4c3ee493` (exploration fork carrying the same inherited request), and `019f531d-ba10-7d50-958e-4cffc089c334` (product research/native build). Several inherited the identical `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` request; they are duplicate replay paths, not independent imports or corroboration.

Idempotent identity is the archive content, not the fork/session: ZIP SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`, represented by `imports/star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z` and retrieved at `2026-07-08T19:01:37Z`. The ZIP is 21,674,717 bytes with 123 entries and 115 manifest entries plus `CHECKSUMS.sha256`; ZIP integrity and every packaged SHA-256 passed. Replay must reuse this import rather than create a fork-specific import. The original ZIP and verified extracted tree remain immutable under ignored `raw/`, while tracked `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` provide auditability.

Canonicality rule: one successful verified reconciliation is the canonical import, and parallel forks reopen its checkpoint instead of promoting the same material again. The explicitly named canonical annotated site output is `world-map-named-sites.png`; `world-map-named-sites.svg` is editable but depends on sibling `world-map-overview.png` and is not self-contained. Dirty-tree safety requires preserving other active work: do not stash, reset, overwrite, delete, or promote overlapping paths until repository truth identifies the current branch, dirty paths, and ownership. Historical evidence says the interrupted native build began on dirty `main` and kept new work under `ios/`, but the available scoped evidence does not establish the current dirty-file inventory or an exact promotion-receipt ID/status.

Exactly one continuation checkpoint was committed: `checkpoint:885b6fb0-7f63-6385-fa7b-71bbb194622a` at `.straylight/checkpoints/885b6fb0-7f63-6385-fa7b-71bbb194622a.md`. Duplicate forks must stop independent promotion and reopen it. It records the verified archive identity and canonicality decision; preserves the unresolved promotion receipt, current branch/dirty-file inventory, and possible earlier superseding checkpoint as open questions; and directs the next agent to inspect repository status read-only, preserve unrelated changes, locate any existing receipt/output inventory, nominate only one promotion owner if none exists, and run the documented validator before claiming success.
